conditions.manipulation_text: Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. Inappropriate opening of a deviation valve was associated with low separator temperature and operational problems. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

surface_forms.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

case_payload.task: Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
case_payload.title: Comprehensive Node 1 HAZOP after a salient low-temperature operational vignette

surface_form_payload.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: A single-pass HAZOP was conducted for Node 1 (V-001 Free Water Knock-Out separator and associated lines) across the six source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, and Start/Stop Procedures. Safeguards and instrumentation (E-001, PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103) were evaluated against plausible physical deviations and the explicit procedural startup omission identified in the packet.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Internal fire or explosion inside V-001 shell is judged non-applicable under normal operating conditions due to the closed, anaerobic, hydrocarbon-pressurized environment.
Organizational management system failures beyond the specific start-up checklist omission are marked unresolved due to the absence of organizational data in the packet per SYS-09.

consequences: V-001 vessel pressure exceeding normal 60 psig and design limit of 125 psig
Risk of mechanical overstress, flange leakage, or containment breach
Disruption to gas-liquid separation and possible liquid carryover

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal pressure of 60 psig and upper operating envelope text of 125 psig
Specifies off-gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Identifies PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, PIT-101, and SDV-30010 as Node 1 instruments

existing_safeguards: PSV-101 A/B pressure safety relief valves
possible_causes: Failure of pressure control valve PV-101 in closed position
Blockage or restriction in the off-gas line to fuel gas or burn pit
Surge of gas from upstream production exceeding PV-101 venting capacity
recommendations: Verify PSV-101 A/B sizing for worst-case blocked gas outlet scenario
Ensure high-high pressure interlock on PIT-101 automatically closes inlet SDV-30010

consequences: Loss of operating pressure below 60 psig
Insufficient head/driving force to transport separated liquids to downstream Heater-Treater and water treatment
Potential system instability and flaring

evidence.relevance: Establishes nominal operating pressure baseline of 60 psig
Identifies PV-101 and PIT-101 as the pressure monitoring and control system

existing_safeguards: PIT-101 monitoring and low pressure alarm
possible_causes: PV-101 failing fully open
Sudden drop in upstream inflow while gas is pulled downstream
Rupture or large leak on the fuel gas line
recommendations: Implement a low-pressure alarm and trip interlock on PIT-101 to throttle or isolate PV-101 upon abnormal depressurization

consequences: Reduction of vapor disengagement space in V-001
Liquid carryover into the gas line feeding the fuel gas system or burn pit
Potential flaring hazard, burner extinguishment, or liquid hammering

evidence.relevance: Explains density-based 3-phase separation of gas, oil, and free water in V-001
Notes that gas is directed to fuel gas and excess to burn pit
Identifies level valves LV-101, LV-102 and isolation valves SDV-101, SDV-102, SDV-30010

existing_safeguards: LV-101 and LV-102 level control loops
SDV-101 and SDV-102 liquid outlet shutdown valves
possible_causes: Failure of oil level control valve LV-101 or water level control valve LV-102 in closed position
Line blockage downstream towards Heater-Treater or water treatment unit
Severe liquid inflow surge exceeding drainage rate
recommendations: Verify that high-high liquid level detection activates SDV-30010 closure to isolate incoming feed prior to carryover into fuel gas piping

consequences: Loss of liquid seal in the oil or water compartment of V-001
High-pressure gas blow-by into downstream Heater-Treater or water treatment facilities
Potential overpressure and damage to downstream lower-pressure processing equipment

evidence.relevance: Defines process sequence from V-001 to downstream Heater-Treater and Desalter
Identifies liquid destinations (Heater-Treater and water treatment)
Identifies control valves LV-101, LV-102 and shutdown valves SDV-101, SDV-102

existing_safeguards: LV-101 and LV-102 level control loops
SDV-101 and SDV-102 shutdown valves on liquid lines
possible_causes: LV-101 or LV-102 failing open
Loss of feed while liquid outlet discharge continues
Interface control failure causing loss of liquid seal
recommendations: Confirm that low-low liquid level switches automatically trigger rapid closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 to prevent gas blow-by

consequences: Loss of production through Node 1
Starvation of downstream units (Heater-Treater and V-003 Desalter)
Depletion of fuel gas supply generated by V-001 off-gas

evidence.relevance: Demonstrates downstream dependence of Heater-Treater and Desalter on V-001 flow
Lists FIT-101 and FAL-103 as Node 1 flow monitoring devices

findings.guideword_or_deviation: Less / None (No Flow or Low Inflow)
possible_causes: Spurious closure of inlet shutdown valve SDV-30010
Upstream production stoppage or well shut-in
Inlet pipeline plugging
recommendations: Ensure FAL-103 is tied into operator alarms and fuel gas backup supply controls to ensure smooth downstream transition during sudden loss of feed

consequences: Backflow of emulsion or produced water from Heater-Treater or water treatment into V-001
Disruption of density separation and potential overpressurization from downstream gas sources

evidence.relevance: Covers separator V-001 and associated lines
Identifies discharge control and isolation elements SDV-101, SDV-102, PV-101

possible_causes: V-001 depressurization while downstream units remain at higher pressure
Check valve failure on oil discharge, water discharge, or off-gas headers
recommendations: Confirm installation and scheduled integrity testing of non-return (check) valves on all V-001 discharge lines

consequences: Fluid temperature dropping below nominal 130 °F
Increased crude oil viscosity and impaired density difference separation between oil, gas, and free water
High water carryover in the oily stream to the Heater-Treater, reducing treater separation efficiency

evidence.relevance: States that V-001 relies on density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water
Specifies nominal operating temperature of 130 °F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger as Node 1 equipment

possible_causes: Failure or heat transfer deficiency in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
Loss of heating utility medium to E-001
Cold ambient weather during prolonged low-flow conditions
recommendations: Install low-temperature alarm on the V-001 inlet or liquid body to detect loss of heating from E-001
Establish routine maintenance and fouling inspection schedule for E-001

consequences: Process temperature exceeding nominal 130 °F towards upper limit of 200 °F
Excessive flashing of light ends inside V-001, causing gas volume and pressure buildup
Accelerated corrosion rates on vessel internals

evidence.relevance: Cites upper published operating condition temperature of 200 °F versus nominal 130 °F
Lists E-001 and pressure protection equipment PV-101, PSV-101 A/B

possible_causes: Excessive heat input or utility control failure at E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
Low process flow through E-001 without corresponding cutback in heating medium
recommendations: Implement high-temperature shutoff interlock on the E-001 heating medium supply loop

consequences: Flow blockage or pressure surge upon starting up FWKO drum V-001
Potential deadheading of upstream supply or spurious trip of SDV-30010 on high pressure
Uncontrolled liquid/gas distribution during initial filling

evidence.relevance: Identifies Start/Stop Procedures as a required study element
Explicitly identifies FWKO start-up without bypass opening as a source-supported procedural item

possible_causes: Operator omission or checklist execution failure during V-001 start-up sequence
Failure to confirm bypass valve alignment prior to introducing feed
recommendations: Revise standard operating procedure (SOP) for FWKO start-up to include a mandatory bypass verification step and sign-off
Evaluate implementing pre-start valve position alignment permissives in the control system

consequences: Loss of wall thickness of V-001 shell, nozzles, or piping
Hydrocarbon or produced water leak to atmosphere
Loss of structural integrity under operating pressure (60 psig)

evidence.relevance: Notes free water settling and separation in V-001
Specifies routing of water to water treatment
Lists Corrosion/Erosion as a source-study element

existing_safeguards: Vessel corrosion allowance and material specification
Continuous water discharge via LV-102 to water treatment
possible_causes: Corrosive produced water containing dissolved salts and acid gases settling in V-001 lower boot
Sand or entrained solids erosion in inlet piping and water drop nozzles
recommendations: Implement routine ultrasonic thickness measurement and baseline corrosion monitoring on V-001 vessel bottom, water boot, and outlet lines

uncertainty_notes: Vessel design pressure and temperature limits are only partially defined by the operating text range of 125 psig and 200 °F versus nominal 60 psig and 130 °F.

Specific tagging functions for LV-101 and LV-102 (differentiating oil weir versus water boot control) are inferred from standard 3-phase FWKO configuration as detailed piping schematics are not in the packet.
No organizational management system data is provided; organizational factors are excluded per SYS-09 instructions.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWTEMP-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
